Saturday 2 November 2024

To mark the Hindu New Year (Kartik sud 1, Vikram Samvat 2081), a channel has been created to enable all to engage in smruti of vicharan of the Satpurush in the UK and Europe.

This will cover the vicharan of: Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj (1970), Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj (18 visits from 1974 to 2007) and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj (2017 and 2023)

After learning in one of the recent discourses of the Shakotsav celebrated 170 years previously in Loya by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the devotees of London made a sankalp that such a shakotsav be celebrated in London as well.

After due preparations were made, Param Pujya Swamishri went to the Mandir kitchen area around 4.50pm and personally conducted the shak vaghar in three big utensils in which a total of 10 maunds (200kg) of aubergines were prepared. After offering the final product to Harikrishna Maharaj, the devotees partook of this as prasad following the evening sabha.

On this day, Pujya Mahant Swami also travelled to the BAPS Mandir in Leicester to perform pujan of the marble murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

9 November 1997
London, UK

His Majesty King Charles III, formerly known as The Prince of Wales, receives Swamishri at St James’ Palace. 

He writes: "I have especially fond memories of his visit to St. James Palace in 1997, and our conversation about interfaith harmony and world peace. I have been a great admirer of His Holiness's remarkable gift to London in the form of the Neasden Temple - an exquisite and traditional Hindu Mandir. We have also visited the magnificent Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, on our last trip to India. I was particularly impressed by the astonishing efforts that had been made to build Akshardham, whilst at the same time preserving the Vedic architectural principles and traditions. His Holiness's inspiration has not only created these two wonderful landmarks, but has also inspired a vibrant community to lead pious and virtuous lives, following his own life ethos, 'In the joy of others lies our own.'"

1 January 2000.
The turn of the millennium.

Devotees in London gathered on 31 December 1999 at the mandir in London for a special devotional programme to usher in a new year and the new millennium.

After a fun-filled programme, the sabha was connected by phone live in the early hours of the morning to Chennai, where Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj was engaged in his morning walk.

Devotees sitting in London offered their prayers in the form of a prarthna: Mahabalvant maya tamari...

Param Pujya Swamishri then gave live audio blessings to the gathering. An auspicious start to a new millennium.

2 April 1982
London, UK
Pramukh Swami Maharaj performs murti pratishtha of the Hari Mandir in Neasden, London. 

Yogiji Maharaj created the first mandir in the UK in Islington in 1970. Until 1982, the Islington mandir was the home of satsang in London. In 1982, the Neasden Hari Mandir and hall was inaugurated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The Neasden Hari Mandir was to be the home of all satsang activities, seva, bhakti, katha from 1982 until 1995 when the shikharbaddha mandir was created just across the road.

To learn about and watch this historic moment - https://youtu.be/Ofn555225yM?t=4606

11 April to 14 April 1984
Lisbon, Portugal

Forty years ago, during his first vicharan in mainland Europe in 1984, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited Lisbon from 11 April to 14 April and blessed the land of Portugal. 

During the vicharan, the devotees took Swamishri to bless several iconic locations as well as bless the homes of local devotees.

During the evening sabha on 13 April at the Alvalade Church, over 1,200 devotees gathered to have darshan and receive Swamishri’s blessings.

Swamishri's vicharan in Lisbon in 1988 and 2000 further nourished the Satsang, eventually culminating in the murti pratishtha at the new BAPS mandir in 2014 at the hands of Sadguru Pujya Mahant Swami and Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami. This year marks 11 years since the opening of Lisbon Mandir..

28 April 1988
London, UK
Pramukh Swami Maharaj is honoured at the British Parliament. 

In his 9-minute speech, Swamishri spoke about the mahima of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Governor Sir John Malcolm's meeting with Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the work of the paramhansas, and how Bhagwan Swaminarayan worked for peace, morality and the happiness of society. He prayed for the entire British community and for peace to prevail in this country. 

Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Pujya Dharmavatsal Swami also delivered speeches. Pujya Yogicharan Swami recited Sanskrit shloks and the sant mandal sang the bhajan, 'Swaminarayan nam vahalu lage...'.

34 years later on Monday 19 December 2022, the centennial birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj was celebrated with a special commemorative event at the Palace of Westminster, home of the British Parliament. See video and photographs of this event here:  https://www.baps.org/News/2022/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Centennial-Anniversary-Celebrated-at-British-Parliament-22890.aspx

Yogi Jayanti

Happy Birthday Yogi Bapa
Jay Swaminarayan

Today morning, after puja, I remembered you a lot.
You would call me by the name Vinu, and remembered other memories like the mango incident.
I still cannot forget your selfless love.
Your divine murti still instantly appears in my mind.
By meeting you, we are fulfilled.
Today, seeing the satsang in London, all of your wishes can be seen to be fulfilled.
You are the form of God. 
So on this day of Yogi Jayanti, I pray that as per your wish, may unity increase in the whole of BAPS satsang, may all see divinity in one another, and may nobody focus on others' flaws.
May all attain ekantik dharma, and may all become happy physically, financially, and mentally.

Written by Sadhu Keshavjivandas, Jay Swaminarayan with lots of love.

At Thakorbhai's home in Thornton Heath in Surrey, Yogiji Maharaj blesses Thakorbhai in abundance for offering his son to be initiated as a sadhu by Yogiji Maharaj.
--------------
Yogiji Maharaj's love drew many yuvaks, inspiring some to renounce worldly life and become sadhus. One such youth was Kamleshbhai, son of Thakorbhai. 

When the family of Thakorbhai readily gave permission for their middle son to become a sadhu and offered him to Yogiji Maharaj during his stay at their house on 12 June 1970, Yogiji Maharaj remarked, “By offering Kamleshbhai to us, it is greater than giving us one million pounds.”

Kamleshbhai was subsequently initiated by Yogiji Maharaj as a parshad, named Ghanshyam Bhagat, on 14 October 1970 in Gondal on the auspicious day of Sharad Poonam. A short while later, on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi on 31 January 1971 in Gondal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj initiated him as Aksharvihari Swami.

Aksharvihari Swami recalls: "When I had the privilege to see Yogiji Maharaj up close, I was struck by his ever-blissful smiling face, innocent deep eyes, saintliness, and simple, tender behaviour. I was initiated as a parshad by Yogiji Maharaj. Despite us being young, careless, and unreliable, Yogi Bapa was always compassionate and gentle — with a heart even bigger than an affectionate mother.”

Yagneshwar Swami recalls an incident from Sunday 19 June 1977:

We visited Ishwarbhai Master's house in Wembley. Swamishri and the sadhus were to eat in a small kitchen, while around 70–80 devotees had a buffet dinner outside. When Swamishri entered the kitchen, he saw a few youths peeking through the window, calling, “Bapa! Prasad!”

Swamishri signaled Bhaktikishore Swami to serve sweets in the form of pistapak. As Swamishri looked around to find a way to pass the prasad, Bhaktikishore Swami tried to open the window but couldn’t. Swamishri spotted a small opening at the top, tiptoed, and began passing prasad through it.

Soon, more devotees gathered. The sadhus placed wooden stands to support Swamishri. When the pistapak ran out, Swamishri asked for rotlas, broke them into quarters, and continued serving until everyone received prasad.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj decides the land on which to build the first shikkharbaddh mandir in the western world.

A short distance away and a short while previously, he had already conducted the khatmuhrat vidhi at Neasden High School.

However, amidst the dust and heat of Neasden on that summer's day, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's inner eyes spotted the potential of another site before him.

We noticed a simple 'For Sale' sign at the Arlington warehouse.

He saw a grand shikkharbaddh mandir that would be worthy of the home of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj in Great Britain.

Watch the captivating story of this day here: https://youtu.be/fmvEG_qBiec?t=2205

16 June to 5 August 1985

UK

With the blessings and agna of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, a group of sadhus and parshads led by Sadguru Pujya Mahant Swami came to London to oversee the preparations for the upcoming Cultural Festival of India to be celebrated on the grounds of Alexandra Park from 16 July to 18 August 1985.

Pujya Mahant Swami arrived in London on 16 June 1985 and conducted various vidhis and gave invaluable guidance for the set up of the festival site on the grounds of Alexandra Park. He also inspired the volunteers who were tirelessly toiling throughout the day to make the festival a grand success.

Devotees eagerly awaited the arrival of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj in London on 10 July 1985 with preparations for both the CFI and Suvarna Mahotsav in full swing.

On 7 July 1970, after gracing the UK for 46 days, Yogiji Maharaj departed for India. During a flight stopover at Orly Airport in Paris, France, Yogiji Maharaj requested Pujya Pramukh Swami and Pujya Mahant Swami to step foot onto the land of Europe on his behalf, historically marking the first European visit of the Satpurush. See special smruti video above.

Exactly 52 years later, on 7 July 2022 in Ahmedabad, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the shila pujan of the bricks to be ceremoniously placed in the foundation of the new BAPS mandir to be constructed in Paris.

8 JULY 2000
London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj received two Guinness World Records at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. 

1. For building the largest traditional Hindu mandir outside of India. 

2. For performing 355 mandir consecration ceremonies (between April 1971 and May 2000).

This was updated in 2007 when Swamishri was awarded the certificate for creating and consecrating a world-record 713 mandirs.

Until his passing in 2016, over a period of 45 years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj built 2 Akshardham mahamandirs, 37 traditional stone shikharbaddha mandirs and 1,192 hari mandirs (a grand total of 1,231 Hindu mandirs) as well as inspiring thousands of families to install ghar mandirs in their homes.

20 July 1980
London, UK
Shobha Yatra

On Sunday 20 July 1980, the festival marking the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the new hari mandir in Neasden was celebrated with a grand procession through the local streets of Wembley, North London.

During the procession, Swamishri was seated on an elephant with Harikrishna Maharaj on his lap. A short while later, it began to rain and an umbrella was passed to Swamishri. He instinctively used the umbrella to cover Thakorji while he himself was drenched. Seeing Swamishri hold the umbrella in such humble devotion, it seemed as through the procession was only for Harikrishna Maharaj and Swamishri was the charioteer.

Thousands flocked to Queens Park Rangers football stadium, Loftus Road, West London, on the afternoon of 20 July 1985. Everyone was eager to witness the ‘Suvarna Mahotsav’, where Swamishri would be weighed against sugar crystals. 

Having been gifted with the greatest honour one can offer a spiritual master, Swamishri rose to bless the Suvarna Mahotsav congregation with great humility and love, as he revealed, “Firstly, I would like to offer my humble prostrations to the supreme Bhagwan Swaminarayan for this body he has blessed me with, and to Guru Shastriji Maharaj and Guru Yogiji Maharaj, who have blessed me and accepted me as theirs. I offer my deep prostrations to my gurus as they have blessed me with this opportunity of serving you all.”

Leicester, UK
Murti Pratishtha

Satsang had been established in Leicester following Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970, and further consolidated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vicharan in 1974. The local devotees were inspired by Swamishri to search for a place to worship.

On the morning of Sunday 24 July 1977, Swamishri joined 70 devotees in the yagna ceremony, before consecrating the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj at the new mandir in Leicester on 148 Doncaster Road, the third Akshar-Purushottam mandir in the UK. [The murtis were later moved to larger premises at 3 St. James Street in 1979, where they remained until the opening of the new mandir in Leicester on 9 October 2011.]

30 July 1977
Adhik Shravan sud 15, VS 2033
Wellingborough, UK

On Saturday 30 July (Adhik Shravan sud Punam), Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated a new mandir in Wellingborough, the third BAPS Swaminarayan mandir to be consecrated in a short span of 15 days.

The pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Radha-Krishna Bhagwan and the Guru Parampara were part of a grand procession through the streets of Wellingborough. 

Hundreds of devotees gathered to make history as the first Hindu mandir in Wellingborough was opened at humble premises on Mill Road.

What began with a small group of devotees gathering in 1972, and then a small hari mandir on 16 Mill Road, has now, after the installation of the ‘Akshar Deri’ at the newly built mandir in 2009, become a pilgrimage centre for the UK devotees, and the venue for the annual Akhand Dhun.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departs from Ahmedabad for Robbinsville, USA with transit stop in Brussels, Belgium

Defying everyone's expectations and despite his advanced age and fragile health, Pramukh Swami Maharaj decides to come to Robbinsville for the mandir murti pratishtha and bless the land of Swaminarayan Akshardham in North America.

Sunday 20 August 1995 
Shravan vad 10
London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London, the first traditional Hindu temple in the west.

It had been 25 years since Yogiji Maharaj had declared his divine wish for a traditional mandir in London, spoken at the time of the opening of the small mandir in Islington in June 1970.

It had been 23 years since Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself had proclaimed a majestic vision for London, in 1972, in Piplana. 

For 10 years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had led an arduous search for land, and for 3 years, he had inspired hundreds of devotees and volunteers to contribute and serve selflessly.  

Today was a moment that would forever change the history of Sanatan Hindu Dharma in the western world, one that would be forever etched in the minds and hearts of thousands.

On Sunday 15 September 1974, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ceremoniously installed the new murtis at Islington Mandir.

24 September 2017
London, UK
Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Chhavani

An all-day ‘chhavani’ (spiritual camp of discourses) on the fundamental principles of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan (upasana) was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj and senior swamis at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.

Mahant Swami Maharaj had expressed his wish for this special programme to be organised and personally encouraged everyone to attend. He drew upon the four-month chhavani that had been held in Vartal, India, during the time of Gunatitanand Swami and gave his blessings for a similar day of spiritual enrichment in London.

Such was Swamishri’s enthusiasm for Akshar-Purushottam Darshan that he presided over the day’s discourses for over seven hours in total and himself spoke four times.

6 October 1990
South London Crematorium, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj attended the funeral of Jaykrishnabhai and personally performed the final rites. Amid an intense vicharan schedule, he fulfilled a devotee’s wish. After performing his morning puja in Colchester, he travelled nearly two hours to reach the crematorium.

Mahant Swami Maharaj writes in Divine Memories 4 that Swamishri’s love “is not a topic of discussion, but a subject of experience… Only experience allows us to comprehend it fully.” He adds: “Just as a true mother engulfs her child with selfless love, Swamishri also greets everyone he meets with selfless love. He feels overjoyed to be helpful to someone, to please someone, to serve someone. In doing so, he completely forgets about his own bodily needs. By any means, he loves; he cares; he redeems.”

These words come to life in this prasang.

10 April 1984
Netherlands

42 years ago today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced The Netherlands. He blessed the home of a devotee named Jeanette Groenen, a Dutch lady who had made a wish during the bicentenary birth celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in 1981 that Pramukh Swami visit her home. This was fulfilled by Swamishri exactly three years later.

This video above is her memory of this magical surprise, which fell on the auspicious day of Swaminarayan Jayanti & Rama Navmi.

11 April to 14 April 1984
Lisbon, Portugal

Forty years ago, during his first vicharan in mainland Europe in 1984, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited Lisbon from 11 April to 14 April and blessed the land of Portugal. 

During the vicharan, the devotees took Swamishri to bless several iconic locations as well as bless the homes of local devotees.

During the evening sabha on 13 April at the Alvalade Church, over 1,200 devotees gathered to have darshan and receive Swamishri’s blessings.

Swamishri's vicharan in Lisbon in 1988 and 2000 further nourished the Satsang, eventually culminating in the murti pratishtha at the new BAPS mandir in 2014 at the hands of Sadguru Pujya Mahant Swami and Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami. This year marks 12 years since the opening of Lisbon Mandir.

28 April 1988
London, UK
Pramukh Swami Maharaj is honoured at the British Parliament. 

In his 9-minute speech, Swamishri spoke about the mahima of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Governor Sir John Malcolm's meeting with Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the work of the paramhansas, and how Bhagwan Swaminarayan worked for peace, morality and the happiness of society. He prayed for the entire British community and for peace to prevail in this country. 

Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Pujya Dharmavatsal Swami also delivered speeches. Pujya Yogicharan Swami recited Sanskrit shloks and the sant mandal sang the bhajan, 'Swaminarayan nam vahalu lage...'.

34 years later on Monday 19 December 2022, the centennial birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj was celebrated with a special commemorative event at the Palace of Westminster, home of the British Parliament. See video and photographs of this event here:  https://www.baps.org/News/2022/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Centennial-Anniversary-Celebrated-at-British-Parliament-22890.aspx

London
16.05.2023
Tuesday
Yogi Jayanti

Happy Birthday Yogi Bapa
Jay Swaminarayan

Today morning, after puja, I remembered you a lot.
You would call me by the name Vinu, and remembered other memories like the mango incident.
I still cannot forget your selfless love.
Your divine murti still instantly appears in my mind.
By meeting you, we are fulfilled.
Today, seeing the satsang in London, all of your wishes can be seen to be fulfilled.
You are the form of God. 
So on this day of Yogi Jayanti, I pray that as per your wish, may unity increase in the whole of BAPS satsang, may all see divinity in one another, and may nobody focus on others' flaws.
May all attain ekantik dharma, and may all become happy physically, financially, and mentally.

Written by Sadhu Keshavjivandas, Jay Swaminarayan with lots of love.

For the opening of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Islington, London, Yogiji Maharaj graced the land of UK from 23 May to 7 July 1970 for 46 days and left lasting memories for countless haribhaktas and built the foundation for the development of satsang in UK-Europe.

At Thakorbhai's home in Thornton Heath in Surrey, Yogiji Maharaj blesses Thakorbhai in abundance for offering his son to be ordained as a sadhu by Yogiji Maharaj.
--------------
Yogiji Maharaj's love drew many yuvaks, inspiring some to renounce worldly life and become sadhus. One such youth was Kamleshbhai, son of Thakorbhai. 

When the family of Thakorbhai readily gave permission for their middle son to become a sadhu and offered him to Yogiji Maharaj during his stay at their house on 12 June 1970, Yogiji Maharaj remarked, “By offering Kamleshbhai to us, it is greater than giving us one million pounds.”

Kamleshbhai was subsequently ordained by Yogiji Maharaj as a parshad, named Ghanshyam Bhagat, on 14 October 1970 in Gondal on the auspicious day of Sharad Punam. A short while later, on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi on 31 January 1971 in Gondal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ordained him as Aksharviharidas Swami.

Aksharvihari Swami recalls: "When I had the privilege to see Yogiji Maharaj up close, I was struck by his ever-blissful smiling face, innocent deep eyes, saintliness, and simple, tender behaviour. I was ordained as a parshad by Yogiji Maharaj. Despite us being young, careless, and unreliable, Yogi Bapa was always compassionate and gentle — with a heart even bigger than an affectionate mother.”

Yagneshwar Swami recalls an incident from Sunday 19 June 1977:

We visited Ishwarbhai Master's house in Wembley. Swamishri and the sadhus were to eat in a small kitchen, while around 70–80 devotees had a buffet dinner outside. When Swamishri entered the kitchen, he saw a few youths peeking through the window, calling, “Bapa! Prasad!”

Swamishri signaled Bhaktikishore Swami to serve sweets in the form of pistapak. As Swamishri looked around to find a way to pass the prasad, Bhaktikishore Swami tried to open the window but couldn’t. Swamishri spotted a small opening at the top, tiptoed, and began passing prasad through it.

Soon, more devotees gathered. The sadhus placed wooden stands to support Swamishri. When the pistapak ran out, Swamishri asked for rotlas, broke them into quarters, and continued serving until everyone received prasad.

London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj decides the land on which to build the first shikkharbaddh mandir in the western world.

A short distance away and a short while previously, he had already conducted the khatmuhrat vidhi at Neasden High School.

However, amidst the dust and heat of Neasden on that summer's day, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's inner eyes spotted the potential of another site before him.

We noticed a simple 'For Sale' sign at the Arlington warehouse.

He saw a grand shikkharbaddh mandir that would be worthy of the home of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj in Great Britain.

16 June to 5 August 1985

UK

With the blessings and agna of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, a group of sadhus and parshads led by Sadguru Pujya Mahant Swami came to London to oversee the preparations for the upcoming Cultural Festival of India to be celebrated on the grounds of Alexandra Park from 16 July to 18 August 1985.

Pujya Mahant Swami arrived in London on 16 June 1985 and conducted various vidhis and gave invaluable guidance for the set up of the festival site on the grounds of Alexandra Park. He also inspired the volunteers who were tirelessly toiling throughout the day to make the festival a grand success.

Devotees eagerly awaited the arrival of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj in London on 10 July 1985 with preparations for both the CFI and Suvarna Mahotsav in full swing.

8 JULY 2000
London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj received two Guinness World Records at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. 

1. For building the largest traditional Hindu mandir outside of India. 

2. For performing 355 mandir consecration ceremonies (between April 1971 and May 2000).

This was updated in 2007 when Swamishri was awarded the certificate for creating and consecrating a world-record 713 mandirs.

Until his passing in 2016, over a period of 45 years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj built 2 Akshardham mahamandirs, 37 traditional stone shikharbaddha mandirs and 1,192 hari mandirs (a grand total of 1,231 Hindu mandirs) as well as inspiring thousands of families to install ghar mandirs in their homes.

Suvarna Mahotsav 
London, UK 

Thousands flocked to Queens Park Rangers football stadium, Loftus Road, West London, on the afternoon of 20 July 1985. Everyone was eager to witness the ‘Suvarna Mahotsav’, where Swamishri would be weighed against sugar crystals. 

Having been gifted with the greatest honour one can offer a spiritual master, Swamishri rose to bless the Suvarna Mahotsav congregation with great humility and love, as he revealed, “Firstly, I would like to offer my humble prostrations to the supreme Bhagwan Swaminarayan for this body he has blessed me with, and to Guru Shastriji Maharaj and Guru Yogiji Maharaj, who have blessed me and accepted me as theirs. I offer my deep prostrations to my gurus as they have blessed me with this opportunity of serving you all.”

Satsang had been established in Leicester following Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970, and further consolidated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vicharan in 1974. The local devotees were inspired by Swamishri to search for a place to worship.

On the morning of Sunday 24 July 1977, Swamishri joined 70 devotees in the yagna ceremony, before consecrating the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj at the new mandir in Leicester on 148 Doncaster Road, the third Akshar-Purushottam mandir in the UK. [The murtis were later moved to larger premises at 3 St. James Street in 1979, where they remained until the opening of the new mandir in Leicester on 9 October 2011.]

30 July 1977
Adhik Shravan sud 15, VS 2033
Wellingborough, UK

On Saturday 30 July (Adhik Shravan sud Punam), Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated a new mandir in Wellingborough, the third BAPS Swaminarayan mandir to be consecrated in a short span of 15 days.

The pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Radha-Krishna Bhagwan and the Guru Parampara were part of a grand procession through the streets of Wellingborough. 

Hundreds of devotees gathered to make history as the first Hindu mandir in Wellingborough was opened at humble premises on Mill Road.

What began with a small group of devotees gathering in 1972, and then a small hari mandir on 16 Mill Road, has now, after the installation of the ‘Akshar Deri’ at the newly built mandir in 2009, become a pilgrimage centre for the UK devotees, and the venue for the annual Akhand Dhun.

5 August 1985 
Adhik Shravan Vad 5, VS 2041 
Alexandra Park, London

20 July 1985 became a part of BAPS history as Queens Park Rangers Stadium witnessed the first ever Suvarna Mahotsav held to honour Pramukh Swami Maharaj. 

The volunteers had worked hard for several months in planning and setting up the festival, and for them this was going to be the ultimate experience.

However, at Swamishri’s wish, they stayed at the Cultural Festival of India grounds at Alexandra Park to run the exhibitions, food stalls, and other departments. 

The moment of supreme joy arrived at QPR Stadium. Swamishri had been honoured and thousands cheered his name and echoed cries of jubilation.

When the celebrations were over, a sadhu asked Swamishri, “What were you thinking while being weighed?” “I was thinking about the yuvaks who were doing seva back at Ally Pally.”

Swamishri’s response was instant and thought-provoking. It is impossible to think of others while one is being showered with such honour and praise.

A few days later, on 5 August, Swamishri, out of sheer compassion, arranged for a special festival for the volunteers.

The vibrations from the voices of the sadhus and parshads singing could be felt in each and every person's heart, as Swamishri plucked people from the crowd to join in a dance at the end of the special Suvarna Mahotsav programme arranged exclusively for the volunteers.

The few precious seconds previously witnessed at QPR Stadium when Swamishri had danced before departing, were brought back again. This time, his beloved volunteers were much closer and, for them, Swamishri danced a little longer. 

Unbelievable scenes of jubilation, unimaginable atmosphere and bliss... 

This was how Swamishri rewarded those volunteers who had stayed back to serve at the CFI grounds at Alexandra Park.

Sunday 20 August 1995 
Shravan vad 10
London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London, the first traditional Hindu temple in the west.

It had been 25 years since Yogiji Maharaj had declared his divine wish for a traditional mandir in London, spoken at the time of the opening of the small mandir in Islington in June 1970.

It had been 23 years since Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself had proclaimed a majestic vision for London, in 1972, in Piplana. 

For 10 years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had led an arduous search for land, and for 3 years, he had inspired hundreds of devotees and volunteers to contribute and serve selflessly.  

Today was a moment that would forever change the history of Sanatan Hindu Dharma in the western world, one that would be forever etched in the minds and hearts of thousands.

51 YEARS AGO

Sunday 15 September 1974
London, UK

On Sunday 15 September 1974, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ceremoniously installed the new murtis at Islington Mandir.

Yogiji Maharaj had inaugurated the mandir four years earlier in 1970, consecrating small murtis brought from Kampala, Uganda.

In 1974, Pramukh Swami Maharaj consecrated the murtis that had previously been installed by Yogiji Maharaj in Tororo, Uganda, in 1960.

6 October 1990
South London Crematorium, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj attended the funeral of Jaykrishnabhai and personally performed the final rites. Amid an intense vicharan schedule, he fulfilled a devotee’s wish. After performing his morning puja in Colchester, he travelled nearly two hours to reach the crematorium.

Mahant Swami Maharaj writes in Divine Memories 4 that Swamishri’s love “is not a topic of discussion, but a subject of experience… Only experience allows us to comprehend it fully.” He adds: “Just as a true mother engulfs her child with selfless love, Swamishri also greets everyone he meets with selfless love. He feels overjoyed to be helpful to someone, to please someone, to serve someone. In doing so, he completely forgets about his own bodily needs. By any means, he loves; he cares; he redeems.”

These words come to life in this prasang.

🎥 Watch eyewitness testimony and footage of this prasang: https://youtu.be/udFCkI3KBVw?t=1654
